10.1021_acs.jpclett.6c02441: Cu-based single-atom alloys (SAAs), particularly those containing Fe or Co, have been reported to enhance methane formation during electrochemical CO2 reduction, but whether isolated metal dopants act as direct reaction sites remains unresolved. Using Cu(111)-based SAA terrace models, we show that the isolated dopant sites examined remain accessible under reductive conditions. However, neither these dopant sites nor nearby Cu sites improve the adsorbate-mediated CO2-to-CH4 pathway relative to Cu(111), challenging the conventional intermediate-binding picture. For CuCo SAA, explicit-water AIMD simulations reveal that Co instead polarizes adjacent water into an O-H-elongated prereactive configuration. The water-dissociation barrier consequently decreases from 1.12 eV on Cu(111) to 0.67 eV, and the promotional effect persists when *CO binds to Co. These results identify Co-mediated interfacial proton supply as a mechanism beyond carbon-intermediate binding and suggest that interfacial water activation should be considered alongside adsorbate binding when evaluating Cu-based SAA catalysts.
10.1038_s41560-026-02068-9: The envisaged breakthrough of perovskite photovoltaic technologies demands rapid advances in scalable and robust high-throughput fabrication methods. Here we present close-space sublimation (CSS) as a vacuum-based, industrially relevant deposition method for the conversion of sublimed PbI 2 inorganic scaffolds into high-quality wide-bandgap perovskite absorbers (MAPb(I 0.79 Br 0.21 ) 3 , 1.64 eV), employing a reusable mixed-halide organic source for stable bandgap control. We provide mechanistic insights into the substitution-reaction-limited CSS process and achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of up to 18.5% for fully vacuum-processed p–i–n single-junction devices. Monolithic integration in tandem solar cells onto planar, nano- and micro-textured silicon bottom cells reveals consistent optoelectronic and morphological properties across all configurations without requiring adjustments of deposition parameters, as corroborated by comprehensive characterization techniques. The resulting perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells reach PCEs up to 24.3%, with minimal variation across the different bottom cells. Our findings highlight the broad process window and versatility of CSS, positioning it as an industry-suitable deposition method for solvent-free high-throughput fabrication.
10.31635_ccschem.025.202505992: Using fluorine as a partial substitute for oxygen shows great potential to improve the high-voltage stability of Na-layered oxide cathodes.However, the popular NaF-based fluorine doping technique suffers from severe Na and F evaporation during high-temperature synthesis, yielding Na-and Fdeficient cathodes with impurities.Herein, we propose a fluorinating cathode strategy that relies on the high evaporation enthalpy of the fluoride source to achieve effective fluoridation without significant F volatilization.CaF 2 , featuring higher evaporation enthalpy, is selected and achieves simultaneous modification of Na and O sites.The resultant pure O3 phase Na 0.94 Ca 0.03 Ni 0.3 Fe 0.3 Mn 0.3 Cu 0.05- Ti 0.05 O 1.94 F 0.06 cathode with higher F content exhibits highly reversible O3-P3-OP2 phase transitions with minimal cell volume variation and reduced interfacial side reactions at high voltage.Consequently, the cathode delivers an initial capacity of 150.1 mAh g -1 and maintains good capacity retention over 1000 cycles.This work offers a novel fluorine doping strategy via fluoride with high evaporation enthalpy to achieve high-voltage stability of layered oxides.
